title: Inflation is falling. Do prices fall?
hook: Inflation drops every year for five years. What happens to what a basket costs?

knows: inflation is the yearly rise in prices (inflation-halves-cash)
doesNotKnow: that inflation is a rate of change, so 'inflation is falling' means prices rise more slowly, not that they come down; prices fall only when the rate goes below zero

misconception: Inflation is coming down, so prices will come back down.
objective: The learner can explain that inflation falling from 8% to 2% over five years still raises a $100 basket to $125.08, because inflation is the rate prices rise at, not their level; at 0% the price stays put and only a negative rate lowers it.

claims.text: With yearly rates of 8%, 6%, 4%, 3% and 2%, each applied to last year's price, a $100 basket costs 108.00, 114.48, 119.06, 122.63 and then $125.08.
Inflation is how fast prices rise, not how high they are, so a falling rate means slower rises.
claims.source: Definition used by the lesson (stage chip 'Each year's rate applies to last year's price'): the rate is the yearly percentage change of the price level; a smaller positive rate still multiplies the price by more than 1.
claims.note: Definition, not a source: the stage chip sets the rule (each year's rate applies to last year's price), so the rate is the yearly percentage change of the level and any rate above 0 multiplies the price by more than 1. Verified as the lesson's own definition.

claims.text: A sixth year at 0% leaves the basket at $125.08; it does not go back.
claims.source: 125.0836 × (1 + 0) = 125.0836: a zero rate of change leaves the level unchanged. Demo.tsx y6Price(0).
claims.note: Derivation: 125.0836 x (1 + 0) = 125.0836, shown $125.08. The 'zero' milestone is required, so the reveal's sentence always matches a bar the learner saw.

claims.text: A sixth year at −1% lowers the basket to $123.83: prices fall only when the rate goes below zero.
claims.source: 125.0836 × 0.99 = 123.8328; for any rate i ≥ 0, p × (1 + i) ≥ p, so the level falls only if i < 0. Demo.tsx y6Price(-1).
claims.note: Derivation: 125.0836 x 0.99 = 123.8328, shown $123.83; p(1 + i) >= p for every i >= 0, so only i < 0 lowers the level. The 'negative' milestone is required.

claims.text: The rates are made up, not any country's data and not a forecast.
claims.source: Lesson rule; the rates are the brief's illustrative path (Demo.tsx RATES); reveal's last sentence.
claims.note: Lesson rule: RATES is the brief's illustrative path; the reveal says 'Made-up rates, not a forecast'.

recall.question: Inflation was 5% last year and is 1% this year. Over this year, what did prices do on average?
options: They went up, but more slowly
recall.why: Inflation is the rate prices rise at. A fall from 5% to 1% means prices still rose, by 1%, only more slowly; they fall only when inflation is below zero.
